reading.body:
FDD ACTION filed 8 Lobbying Disclosure Act reports naming AI, and those filings name 14 separate bills, which shows the client's AI lobbying is spread across many pieces of legislation rather than concentrated on one.

The filings name nine lobbyists. Matthew Reid Zweig and Nicholas Stewart appear on 8 filings each, Tyler Stapleton on 7, and the rest on between 3 and 6. That is a broad team relative to the filing count, and it suggests AI is one issue among several this client covers rather than a single dedicated campaign.

Fourteen bills is a wide legislative footprint for 8 filings. AI policy is being written across many separate vehicles, not one comprehensive bill, and a client that wants to shape it has to track all of them. This is the political layer that sits above compute and power. The buildings and the grid set the physical limits on AI scaling, and the rules written in these bills set what can be built and where.

The data does not say what FDD ACTION argued, only that it reported lobbying on AI. It does not give dollar amounts, the dates of the filings, or the subject matter of the 14 bills. The bill numbers are listed without titles, so a reader cannot tell from this data alone which ones concern data centers, energy, or procurement.

summary: FDD ACTION filed 8 Lobbying Disclosure Act reports on AI held by this site. Its clients, the lobbyists named on those filings and the AI bills they name are below. LDA registrant id 401105458.
